flawed_step: Lines 0551-0559 (the asserted bound at line 0558: |M_chi(x,y_0)| << x e^{-c(log x)^{3/5}(log_(2) x)^{-1/5}} for X^c << x << X, justified only as 'By an argument similar to that of Koukoulopoulos'). This is the load-bearing input to the unconditional Theorem 3 (beta_0 <= 1 - c/log q) at line 0562.
counterexample: Circularity witness supplied by the paper's own computation: for a real primitive chi with L(beta_0,chi)=0, the Mellin transform at line 0487 has a pole at s=1+beta_0 with positive residue, and lines 0505-0513 derive U >> X^{1+beta_0}/log y_0, hence integral_1^X |M_chi(x,y_0)| dx >> X^{1+beta_0}/(q^{3/2} log y_0). If beta_0 = 1 - delta with delta <= c'/log q (exactly the Siegel zero the theorem is supposed to exclude), then with the paper's calibration log q ≍ (log X)^{2/5}(log_(2)X)^{1/5} one has x^{beta_0-1} = e^{-delta log x} >> e^{-c(log x)^{3/5}(log_(2)x)^{-1/5}} throughout X^c << x << X, so the asserted estimate at 0558 fails for precisely the characters at issue. The bound is therefore not a consequence of Koukoulopoulos-type pretentious arguments (which either exclude the exceptional character or carry an explicit x^{beta_0} term); it is logically equivalent to the conclusion beta_0 <= 1 - c/log q.
reasoning_summary: Steps verified as correct before the failure: (i) Theorem 1 (inversion formula, lines 0165-0183 and 0411-0429) states exactly the Dirichlet inverse of alpha -- beta(n) = sum_k (-1)^k alpha(n_1)...alpha(n_k)/alpha(1)^{k+1} over factorizations into k factors > 1; the extra exclusion n_i != n is vacuous for k >= 2, and the k=1 term matches. Signs via (-alpha(1))^k are correct. (ii) The Cramer's-rule proof sketch (0439-0467) has a terse and imprecisely stated row-reduction step (multiplying rows by S_i changes the determinant, which is not tracked), but the resulting formula is correct; I checked the minor A_{4,1} for X=6 directly and got beta(4) = -(alpha(2)^2+alpha(4)), matching the formula. (iii) The numerical example (0348-0408) checks out: matrix entries alpha(n)=log n - d(n) are right, and all six solution coefficients, including beta(6) = -2log2 log3 + 3log2 + 3log3 - 4, agree with the formula. (iv) The Euler-product identity (0202-0205) and the claim U(X) = sum_{n<=X} alpha(n,y) M(X/n,y) (0209): the coefficient function of M(.,y) has Dirichlet series (1-2^{-s}) prod_{p>y}(1-p^{-s}) = (1/zeta(s)) prod_{3<=p<=y}(1-p^{-s})^{-1}, no double counting occurs since P^-(n)>y forces n odd, and the alpha(.,y) series is zeta(s) prod_{p<=y}(1-p^{-s}); the product is 1-2^{-s}, whose summatory function is U. Correct. (v) The inversion output (0214): U(X/n)=1 iff X/2 < n <= X, giving the stated range floor(X/2)+1 .. floor(X). Correct. (vi) beta(n,y) = sum_{k=1}^{Omega(n)} (-1)^k d_k^*(n,y) (0218) follows because alpha(n_i,y)=1 for all factors iff n is y-rough. Correct. (vii) The truncation remark (0222) and the binomial recursion d_k^* = d_k' - k d_{k-1}^* - C(k,2) d_{k-2}^* - ... (0227) are correct (standard inclusion of positions carrying factors > 1), and hence F_{l,y}(s) is a linear combination of zeta^k(s) prod_{p<=y}(1-p^{-s})^k (0229). (viii) In Section 4 the analytic machinery checks out: g_chi is entire for even primitive chi (trivial zeros at s=1,-1,-3 cancel the denominator factors); the Mellin formula (0487) is correct with the chi(2)=1 twist; the contour shift to sigma = 1+beta_0-1/log y_0 crosses only s=1+beta_0 and the residue evaluation (0509-0511) is right, giving U >> X^{1+beta_0}/log y_0; the sigma=lambda bound |r_lambda(H)| <= e^{-lambda(|H|-1)} for H<=-2 and the resulting tail bound e^{lambda+4}/(lambda-2) << X (0517-0529) are correct; the functional-equation/Stirling bound L(-1+it,chi) << q^{3/2}|t|^{3/2} and the resulting |r_lambda(H)| << q^{3/2}, |U| << q^{3/2} int_1^X |M_chi| (0532-0548) are correct. The chain fails at 0551-0559. Two weaker gaps noted earlier but not counted as certain failures: the 'level' definition (0253-0256) states the bounds only at x while the deduction also needs them at x/2, and Theorem 2 (0274-0284) is asserted with no proof ('one could infer, using methods of Pintz') and is explicitly conditional on the unproved level hypothesis (0244-0251), which the author himself concedes is not established ('the residue term is quite complicated'). The decisive defect is that Theorem 3, stated unconditionally, rests on an unproved estimate that is equivalent to its own conclusion; the additional claim at 0287-0293 that non-principal chi lets one circumvent the Landau-Siegel zero 'since there is no residue term' is the source of the error -- the obstruction is not a residue at s=1 but the pole of 1/L(s,chi) at s=beta_0, which the paper's own Section 4 exploits.
